subtype: Approach: trusting a caller who knows some personal details [Pitfall]
passage: Wednesday night. I feel sick. A man phoned this evening and said he was from the scholarship office. He knew my school's name. He knew Abbu's name. So I thought he must be real, and I stopped being careful. He asked my class, my date of birth, Abbu's phone number, which bank we use. I told him everything because he was so kind and said he was just helping. Then he said a code would arrive and I should read it out. My hand was already on the phone screen when my brother Kunal came in and said, “Who is that? Hang up!” I did. I don't know what I gave away. Tomorrow I have to tell Abbu. — Farida

qa.q: What details did the caller already know?
qa.a: The school's name and Abbu's name.

qa.q: How does Farida feel at the end of the entry?
qa.a: Sick with worry and ashamed: Farida does not know what was given away.

qa.q: What could Farida do next, and why?
qa.a: Tell Abbu and the family straight away so the bank can be warned, since the details already given could be misused.

qa.q: How does the call look to Kunal, who walks in?
qa.a: Kunal hears a stranger asking a sibling for a code, recognises the danger at once and tells them to hang up.

grounding: A student trusts a caller who knows the school name and the father's name, and keeps sharing information to be helpful.

subtype: Approach: trusting a caller who knows some personal details [Pitfall]
passage:
Kavitha: weird call today. some man from “Papa's bank”
Swati: ok??
Kavitha: he knew my school name AND Papa's full name so I thought it was real
Kavitha: he said they're updating records and asked Papa's birthday, his other number, which branch
Kavitha: I told him. I was trying to be helpful
Swati: wait. how would a bank know your SCHOOL
Kavitha: idk... it's on my profile I guess. and Papa's name is on the school website for the parents' committee
Swati: so anyone could know those
Kavitha: oh no
Kavitha: he's calling Papa's other number now. Papa just messaged asking who gave it out
Swati: tell him everything. like right now
Kavitha: told him. he called the bank from the number on his card and they're watching the account. he's not angry, just says next time hang up and ask him
Swati: glad you told him

qa.q: What two details did the caller already know?
qa.a: Kavitha's school name and Papa's full name.

qa.q: Why did Kavitha trust the caller at first?
qa.a: Kavitha felt reassured because the caller knew real details, and wanted to be helpful, so the questions didn't feel suspicious.

qa.q: What could Kavitha do differently next time a caller knows personal details?
qa.a: Remember that such details are easy to find, share nothing, hang up and ask Papa to call the bank on the card's number.

qa.q: How might Papa feel after the call on his other number?
qa.a: Papa is probably alarmed at first, then relieved that Kavitha told him quickly so he could alert the bank the same day.

grounding: Shows a student trusting a caller because he knows the student's school and father's name, sharing more to be helpful, and the cost that follows.

subtype: Approach: trusting a caller who knows some personal details [Pitfall]
passage:
In their kasba near Satara, Shalini was feeding the goats when a call came about a “girls' scholarship”. The man knew she studied at the zilla parishad high school and that her father was Ramesh Patil. That settled it for her. Who else would know?
He asked for her mother's phone number “for the form”, then the branch where the family kept its account, then her father's mobile number. Shalini answered everything. Her little brother Ojas, listening from the step, said, “Tai, why does a scholarship need Aai's number?” She waved him off.
The next morning Aai got a call demanding a code from her phone to “release the scholarship”. Confused, Aai came to Shalini. Shalini's face went hot. She explained everything, and Aai walked straight to the bank branch in the bazaar with her. The manager blocked any changes and warned them such details are often picked up from school notice boards.

qa.a: Why does a scholarship need Aai's number?

qa.q: What does Shalini's hot face the next morning suggest?
qa.a: It suggests she felt ashamed and alarmed, realising the details she gave so trustingly were being used against her own family.

qa.q: What could Shalini have done when the caller asked for Aai's number?
qa.a: Say she would check with her parents first, hang up, and let them contact the school or the scholarship office directly.

qa.q: How might Ojas see the whole thing?
qa.a: Ojas, whose question was waved off, may feel a little vindicated but mostly worried for Aai.

grounding: Shows a student trusting a caller who knows her school and father's name, then giving out more family details to be helpful, with a costly result.
